claims.quote: Here she will stay a shutterless observatory; a life-boat station; a salvage tug; a court of ultimate appeal-cum-meteorological bureau for three hundred miles in all directions, till Wednesday next when her relief slides across the stars to take her buffeted place.
claims.description: A permanently hovering airship station serves as observatory, lifeboat station, salvage tug, court of appeal and weather bureau for a 300-mile region, relieved weekly.

claims.quote: But that semi-elected, semi-nominated body of a few score of persons of both sexes, controls this planet.
claims.description: A small, partly elected and partly appointed board of men and women that oversees air traffic effectively governs the whole planet.

claims.quote: Theoretically, we do what we please so long as we do not interfere with the traffic AND ALL IT IMPLIES.
claims.description: Personal freedom in this world is limited only by the rule that nobody may interfere with air traffic and everything that depends on it.

claims.quote: Practically, the A. B. C. confirms or annuls all international arrangements and, to judge from its last report, finds our tolerant, humorous, lazy little planet only too ready to shift the whole burden of public administration on its shoulders.
claims.description: The air traffic authority ratifies or cancels all international agreements, and the world's people willingly hand it the whole burden of public administration.

claims.quote: A postal packet's dip-dial records every yard of every run.
claims.description: Mail airships carry an instrument that records the whole flight path on paper tape, like a flight data recorder.

claims.quote: The tapes then go to the A. B. C., which collates and makes composite photographs of them for the instruction of captains.
claims.description: The aviation authority collects recorded flight-path tapes and compiles them into composite images used to train pilots.

claims.quote: And minute by minute our silent clock gives us a sixteen-second mile.
claims.description: The mail airship cruises at one mile every sixteen seconds, about 225 miles per hour.

claims.quote: The old contracts (they will be revised at the end of the year) allow twelve hours for a run which any packet can put behind her in ten.
claims.description: A scheduled transatlantic air-mail run takes about ten hours, under contracts that allow twelve.

claims.quote: So far, we can drag out the dawn to twice its normal length in these latitudes.
claims.description: Aircraft flying west are fast enough to stretch the dawn to twice its normal length at high latitudes.

claims.quote: But some day—even on the Equator—we shall hold the Sun level in his full stride.
claims.description: Aircraft will one day fly west fast enough to keep pace with the Sun even at the Equator, over 1,000 miles per hour.

claims.quote: The deep-sea freighters are rising to lung up after the long night, and the leisurely ocean is all patterned with peacock's eyes of foam.
claims.description: Ocean cargo is carried by fleets of submarine freighters that travel submerged and surface to take in fresh air.

claims.quote: We hoist 'em in sterilized air for a while.
claims.description: Tuberculosis patients are treated aboard hospital airships raised into sterile high-altitude air.

claims.quote: If she was an accident ward she'd be hung up at the eight-thousand-foot level.
claims.description: Flying hospital ships include accident wards that hover at the 8,000-foot level.

claims.quote: How much do the doctors say we've added to the average life of man?
claims.description: Medicine has lengthened average human life expectancy, by thirty years according to the reply.

claims.quote: Trans-Asiatic Directs we met, soberly ringing the world round the Fiftieth Meridian at an honest seventy knots; and white-painted Ackroyd & Hunt fruiters out of the south fled beneath us, their ventilated hulls whistling like Chinese kites.
claims.description: Commercial air liners fly round-the-world routes and ventilated cargo aircraft carry fresh fruit over long distances.

claims.quote: It does not pay to “fly” minerals and oil a mile farther than is necessary; but the risks of transhipping to submersibles in the ice pack off Nain or Hebron are so great that these heavy freighters fly down to Halifax direct, and scent the air as they go.
claims.description: Heavy cargo aircraft carry ore and petroleum by air where moving it to submarine freighters is too risky, although air freight of bulk minerals is costly.

claims.quote: It was curious to watch the action of the holding-down clips all along the frosty river front as the boats cleared or came to rest.
claims.description: Airships dock at receiving towers along a city waterfront and are held in place by mechanical clips.

claims.quote: The warning light for Harmattan winds will be continuous vertical glare (white) on all oases of trans-Saharan N. E. by E. Main Routes.
claims.description: A network of aerial navigation beacons along trans-Saharan air routes signals weather warnings to aircraft.

claims.quote: Wreck of unknown racing-plane, Parden rudder, wire-stiffened xylonite vans, and Harliss engine-seating, sighted and salved 7° 20' S. 18° 41' W. Dec. 15th.
claims.description: Privately built racing aircraft with wire-stiffened celluloid wings fly far out over the ocean.

claims.quote: VALKYRIE (racing plane), A. J. Hartley owner, New York (twice warned).
claims.description: Privately owned racing aircraft are common and their owners can be barred from flight levels for obstructing traffic.

claims.quote: As a consequence, the Northern and North-western upper levels have been practically abandoned, and the high fliers have returned to the ignoble security of the Three, Five, and Six hundred foot levels.
claims.description: Air traffic is organized into designated altitude levels that pilots move between depending on the weather.

claims.quote: We have been treated to the spectacle of what are practically keeled racing-planes driven a clear five foot or more above the water, and only eased down to touch their so-called “native element” as they near the line.
claims.description: Racing boats are really winged craft that skim above the water like hydrofoils or flying boats, prompting new racing rules.

claims.quote: But bat-boat racing has a great future before it.
claims.description: The sport of racing winged boats will keep growing.

claims.quote: Till the 25th October Crete, as all our planet knows, was the sole surviving European repository of “autonomous institutions,” “local self-government,” and the rest of the archaic lumber devised in the past for the confusion of human affairs.
claims.description: Parliaments and local self-government have died out across Europe, surviving in one island only as a tourist show.

claims.quote: The A. B. C. have taken over the administration of Crete on normal lines; and tourists must go elsewhere to witness the “debates,” “resolutions,” and “popular movements” of the old days.
claims.description: The last self-governing territory in Europe is absorbed into the world transport authority's administration after asking to be annexed.
